subject: Post-call: Acme ML discovery — architecture decisions & SDK checklist
messages:
From: Olivia Park <olivia@acme-ml.com>

Cc: acme-ml-ops@acme-ml.com
Date: 2026-01-14T15:12:00-08:00
Subject: Discovery recap + follow-ups (scoring + reranker)

Thanks for a great call today, Sergio — really helpful to see Redwood's runtime. Quick recap from our side and a couple of technical asks so we can scope internal work: 

- Our goal: replace current scoring/rerank pipeline for candidate ranking (short inputs, heavy embedding + cross-encoder rerank). Latency SLO: p95 < 350ms for 4k tokens across embed+rerank.
- Data flow we discussed: ingest -> embedding service -> candidate retrieval -> Redwood for rerank & structured output -> downstream scoring.

Technical asks:
1) SDK + auth patterns: we prefer short-lived credentials from our internal token broker. Can Redwood SDK accept ephemeral tokens and refresh hooks?
2) Routing: we may want to route lower-cost quantized model for bulk offline reranks and a higher-SLO model for live queries. How is policy configured?
3) Structured output: final reranker needs constrained JSON (label + score + debug array). We need guidance on constrained decoding + validation + clear retry semantics if schema fails.

Can you send a short post-call note with owners and next steps? We'll loop in infra and data science once we have an integration checklist.

Thanks,
Olivia
Senior ML Engineer | Acme ML

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-01-15T09:28:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap + follow-ups (scoring + reranker) — tech notes

Quoted: 
> Our goal: replace current scoring/rerank pipeline for candidate ranking (short inputs, heavy embedding + cross-encoder rerank). Latency SLO: p95 < 350ms for 4k tokens across embed+rerank.

Notes / proposed patterns (concise):

1) SDK + auth
- Yes, Redwood SDK supports ephemeral tokens. We surface a token provider interface in our SDK (AuthProvider) that calls your broker and refreshes transparently. Example call pattern: get_token() -> sdk.init(token_provider). We'll attach a snippet in the drive.
- Recommend: issue short-lived tokens ~15m with an HTTP refresh endpoint (standard). For non-browser services, mutual-TLS is also supported if you want higher assurance.

2) Routing policies
- Policy types: latency-first, cost-first, and custom (rules by route, percent traffic, or load). For your use-case:
  - Live requests: route to high-SLO variant (fp16 or 8-bit quantized + AVX-optimized kernels) with strict p95 target.
  - Bulk offline: route to heavily quantized variant for throughput/cost.
- Automatic fallback: if preferred variant is degraded or out of capacity, policy can fall back to compatible model family or queue to reserved capacity.

3) Structured output reliability (this is critical)
- Constrained decoding: use our StructuredOutput schema enforcement layer (beam + token-level constraints). For schemas with simple shape (label:string, score:float, debug:list[string]) we can precompute allowed token prefixes for top-level keys and strongly bias logits.
- Validation flow: 1) Model output -> 2) Fast tokenized schema sanity check (lightweight) -> 3) JSON parse attempt -> 4) Full JSON Schema validation (we recommend using draft-07 subset for performance).
- Retry patterns: define an idempotent retry policy with backoff: 
  - Attempt 1: constrained decode + validation.
  - Attempt 2: if schema parse fails, re-issue with stronger constraints (higher logit bias on expected separators) and include last-good prefix in prompt.
  - Attempt 3: if still failing, fall back to a deterministic extractor (heuristic parser) or a smaller autoregressive deterministic model to map text -> schema, and surface as 'best_effort' with a warning flag.
- Observability: attach per-request schema result code (OK / PARSE_ERROR / VALIDATION_ERROR / FALLBACK_USED) and sample model output for debugging. Ship these as per-route trace fields so your DS can iterate on prompts.

4) Embedding + reranker pattern
- Suggest: pre-filter candidates by dense embeddings (2-5 nearest), then call Redwood reranker with structured output for final ranking. We support one-call rerank + structured result (rank, score, explanation).

5) Perf & profiling notes
- We will provide a small perf harness (post-call) to replay samples at scale to validate p95. Expect to tune batch sizes + KV cache sizing.

I'll drop the code snippets and the recommended schema file in the Drive and attach a diagram.

— Dev
